newsitem.title: ITALY: Concern after cold kills Italian circus hippo.
newsitem.headline: Concern after cold kills Italian circus hippo.

text.p: An animal rights group on Tuesday called for emergency checks in zoos and circuses after a circus hippopotamus called Penelope was killed by sub-zero temperatures gripping most of Italy.

"It is the clearest sign of the great suffering that the recent icy temperatures are causing to exotic animals in circuses throughout Italy," said Adolfo Sansolini, director general of the Italian Anti-Vivisection League.
"We have denounced those responsible for the circus and we ask (health) minister Rosy Bindi to order emergency veterinary checks in all zoos and circuses," he said in a statement.
Penelope, a 12-year-old hippo who was born in captivity, arrived in the north-eastern city of Udine on December 21 as one of the star attractions of the Berlin Circus.

The hippopotamus died on Monday morning of bronchial pneumonia, two days after collapsing when she was let out of her cage for exercise on Saturday in temperatures hovering around -10 degrees celsius (14 degrees Fahrenheit).
Officials said at least three people had died in weather-related incidents across Italy, including a 24-year-old with heart trouble who died while walking his dog.
Heavy snow in north-western Italy continued to cause tailbacks on roads and delays to rail journeys on Tuesday.
The northern city of Milan had 15 cm (six inches) of snow and flights were delayed from both its airports.
Genoa airport, the main one on the north-west Italian Riviera, was closed because of icy conditions on Monday as was Ancona airport on the eastern Adriatic coast.
Further north in the seaside resort of Rimini, people skied on the beach where the sand was covered with snow.

The northern Dolomite region of Carnia, regularly one of the snowiest parts of the country in winter and a popular winter sports destination, was meanwhile complaining of a lack of snow with no major snowfalls since late November.
Some of the pistes on Monte Zoncolan were closed and snow-cannons were being used to make artificial snow.
Tourists in the central Tuscan city of Florence woke up to the sight of snow-covered roofs and monuments.
Car drivers in much of Tuscany, including the provinces of Siena and Arezzo, were using chains on their tyres.
Weather forecasters said on Tuesday the icy conditions in the north were likely to remain but some improvement in central and southern regions hit by snowfalls was expected.
"It seems the worst is past", said a spokesman for the Civil Protection Department in Rome.
